segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Welcome and thank you for joining the Wells Far All line that have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speaker's remarks, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time,

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: simply press star one. If you would like to withdraw your question, press star two.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Please note that today's call is being recorded.

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: I would now like to turn the call over

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: to Mr. John Campbell, Director of Investor Relations. You may begin the conference. Good morning. Thank you for joining our call today. We're CEO Charlie Sharf and our CFO, Mike Sanamisimo, will discuss third quarter results and answer your questions. This call is being recorded. Before we get started, I would like to remind you that our third quarter earnings materials, including the release, financial supplement and presentation deck are available on our website at WellsFargo.com. I'd also like to caution you that we may make forward looking statements during today's call that are subject

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: to risks and uncertainties. Factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from expectations are detailed in our SEC filings, including the form AK filed today containing our earnings materials. Information about a non-GAP financial measures referenced, including a reconciliation of those measures to GAP measures, can also be found in our SEC filings and the earnings materials available on our website. I will now turn the call over to Charlie. Thanks, John. I'm going to provide some comments about our results and the momentum we see across all our businesses. I'll then turn the call over to Mike to review third quarter results in more detail before we take your questions.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Let me start with slide two of the presentation deck. Our third quarter results reflected broad-based growth, higher earnings and stronger returns. Earnings per share grew to $1.87 in the third quarter, up 13% from a year ago. Our ROTCE increased from 14.7% during the first nine months of 2025 to 16.2% during the same period this year and 16.3% this quarter. Revenue grew 2% versus the prior year with growth across all our operating segments, partially offset by lower revenue from our venture capital investments as expected and lower lease income following the sale

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: of our rail car leasing business in the first quarter. Wealth and investment management revenues grew 12%, commercial banking grew 6%, consumer banking and lending grew 5%, and corporate and investment banking grew 3%, with 8% growth in banking, partially offset by modest declines in commercial real estate and markets. Markets was trending towards achieving higher revenue growth but was impacted by a slowdown in the last several weeks of the quarter. However, we still had strong results in equities with revenue increasing 21% from a year ago. Within banking, key areas of investments for us continued to see strong results.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: M&A revenues grew 30% and both equity capital markets and investment grade underwriting fees grew 33% from a year ago. Expenses declined modestly from a year ago. As we have seen in other quarters, higher revenue related expenses, up 15%, were more than offset by a 4% decline in non-revenue related expenses as we continued to invest while increasing efficiency. Headcount continued to decline down 2% in the quarter, 8% year over year and down 30% from its second quarter 2020 peak and has decreased every quarter for the past six years. We generated strong growth in loans and deposits

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: throughout 2026 with third quarter average loans and average deposits both up 11% from a year ago. This growth was broad based with higher loan and deposit balances in both our commercial and consumer businesses. Turning to slide three, we're seeing good performance across each of our businesses. Let me start with consumer banking and lending. Growing consumer primary checking accounts is a key indicator of our progress and this quarter we continued to see momentum. We achieved our 14th consecutive quarter of year over year growth as stronger branch and digital activity, improved product offerings

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and continued investments in marketing have helped drive increased account openings. Our segmented approach to serving affluent customers is also producing strong results. Premier client assets were up 10% from a year ago. We continue to invest in talent with double digit growth in Premier bankers and financial advisors year over year. We've been investing in business banking including adding over 130 business bankers over the past year. We are seeing the initial benefits in our results including checking account openings up 9% and credit cards opening 61% from a year ago. Importantly, we remain disciplined on credit with growth focused primarily on customers

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: with deep existing relationships. Credit card revenue increased from growth a year ago and the second quarter with growth in balances and purchase volume. We opened more than 660,000 new accounts in the third quarter. We again saw strong account openings in our branch channel which has allowed us to reduce our reliance on third party channels. Auto originations grew 15% from a year ago and average balances were up 31%. While we're growing our lending businesses and our customer base is still strong, our underwriting criteria recognized that at some point, consumer credit conditions will weaken. To be clear, we do not see signs of this yet

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: but we know that cycles are inevitable. Turning to wealth and investment management. We know that the wealth and investment management client assets grew 11% from a year ago to $2.5 trillion. Average loan balances increased 16% from a year ago. We identified this as a significant opportunity several years ago and has since enhanced our products and processes to better serve clients and scale the portfolio. We have made significant investments in our technology platforms and expanded investment capabilities with the stronger platform to serve clients. These investments include a new portfolio analysis and client proposal tools for advisors leveraging a Latin wealth technology

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: from BlackRock. We have also increased the number of alternative product offerings in our platform by over 30% this year. In addition, we just launched an AI powered tool for our financial advisors that streamlines routine work and helps them access the information they need to better serve clients. This is the first of several capabilities planned as part of our broader AI strategy in wealth and investment management. Turning to corporate investment banking. In our banking business revenue grew 8% from a year ago and year to date increased 13%. The hiring we've done in investment banking has strengthened our client coverage model and improved our ability to compete which you can see from our improved market share including equity capital market share

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: increasing 84 basis points to 3.9% and increasing our rank in announced US M&A volume to number six up from nine. It's important to note that while we're building our investment banking business and it benefits from strong market environments, its size is still relatively small in the context of the rest of the company. We don't expect it to drive outsized returns in any one period but it has contributed and should continue to contribute to higher returns over time. Market's revenue was down modestly from a year ago. Market conditions were more difficult than prior quarters but we continue to see the benefits of our strategic investments.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Year to date market's revenues increased 14% versus last year. Finally, let me highlight commercial banking where our client acquisition strategy helped to drive strong balance sheet growth. Average loans increased 10% from a year ago reflecting our continued success in attracting new clients and deepening existing relationships supported by our investment in additional bankers. Average deposits increased 16% from a year ago reflecting our deposit gathering initiatives which have attracted deposits from broke new and existing clients even as we've maintained our pricing discipline. We also continue to capture larger share of our commercial banking clients investment banking and markets activities

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: with gross fees 25% higher results highlight the benefits of the investments we've made in our commercial banking franchise which is driving client growth and increasing the diversity of our revenue base. More broadly, we are accelerating our investments in both traditional digital payments and traditional and digital payment solutions for consumers and businesses. We believe tokenized deposits can deliver important benefits for the business. Last month we launched tokenized deposits in our proprietary blockchain platform providing corporate commercial clients with a new way to move money more efficiently. As we expand the platform, clients will be able to move funds 24 hours a day,

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: seven days a week across accounts and borders without changing how they bank with us. Use cases in the US for stable coins remain unclear but we're building solutions to be prepared as opportunities potentially unfold. We along with 20 other international financial institutions are establishing a new company to issue stable coins beginning in the first half of 2027. The product will support wholesale, institutional and retail use cases providing clients with a trusted form of digital money that can improve cross-border payments and facilitate digital asset settlements. We're devoting significant management time and resources to building AI capabilities and dry value.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: The work here is multi-dimensioned. Internally, we're using it to write code faster. Over the past year, this has gone from being a tool to assist programmers to now being able to use autonomous agents when appropriate, to increase capacity and revenue from our branches, to launch marketing campaigns faster, to help identify as well as write and test code to close previously unknown cyber vulnerabilities and to improve and simplify risk management processes. Prove the customer experience, including helping customers complete common banking tasks such as making payments, replacing cards, and getting insights into spending and to accelerate response times

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: for underwriting decisions and customer complaints. We will also evaluate how third-party models and agents can provide value-added capabilities to our clients while at the same time considering the potential risk these tools can introduce for both our clients and Wells Fargo. Our focus was recently recognized in the Evident AI Index for Banks, which independently tracks AI maturity across the world's leading banks. We increased our ranking to number five globally and ranked number three in the US based upon their evaluation of four core pillars, including talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: We're excited by the opportunities AI presents for our clients and our company and we're taking a disciplined approach to managing risk. Looking externally, US economic growth continues to be strong. While uncertainty persists due to sticky inflation, the conflict in the Middle East, persistent fiscal deficits, and volatile energy markets, strong labor markets and wage growth, business investment, productivity investments, infrastructure spending, and a historic wave of technology-related capital expenditures have proven more powerful than many predicted. As a result, real GDP growth continues to track well with the third quarter shaping up to be strong.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: The consumer remains one of the economy's most important sources of resilience, though higher prices continue to weigh on consumer sentiment. Let me highlight our customer trends. Consumer spending remains strong. Debit card spending increased 8% from a year ago with broad-based growth across categories accelerating from the 5% growth rate we saw in the third quarter last year. Credit card spending was up 12% from a year ago. Our growth has been amongst the highest in the industry, driven by strong new account growth. At the same time, consumer credit remains strong with our charge-off ratio down from both the second quarter and a year ago

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and early-stage delinquencies at historically low levels. High-income households continue to benefit from strong asset prices, substantial home equity, and stable labor income. And while lower-income households remain more sensitive to financing costs, inflation, and higher living and fuel expenses, they appear to be stable. Corporate America also continues to demonstrate strength. Our corporate and commercial customers remain in good shape. Loan demand continues and credit remains strong with only 18 basis points of losses in the third quarter and non-approval loans down from both the second quarter and a year ago. While our data is strong, we are conscious of the risks.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Inflation and higher interest rates continue to be headwinds and the longer they persist, the more pressure they could place on both consumers and commercial clients. While markets have been strong, an unexpected or significant movement could filter through the broader economy. And the AI investment cycle has become a complicated, macroeconomic force in its own right. Demand for semiconductors, networking equipment, power generation, data center infrastructure, cooling systems, storage, cybersecurity, and advanced manufacturing equipment continue to surge. The scale of investment here increasingly resembles prior infrastructure booms, creating both significant opportunities,

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: but also risks given the significant leverage used to finance the build-out and the upward pressure on prices in selected industries. Having said this, the strength of the economy and the positive forces from these investments have thus far outweighed the potential downside. Before I conclude, I wanna thank Derek Flowers, our Chief Risk Officer for his leadership in strengthening our risk and control framework and culture to position Wells Fargo for continued growth. As we announced last month, Derek plans to retire early next year and he will work closely with Scott Powell, our Chief Operating Officer to support the smooth transition when Scott assumes the Chief Risk Officer role.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: As I close, I'll leave you with a few final thoughts. Our progress towards building a growing, high returning company continues. Our ROTCD continues to increase and is getting closer to our 17 to 18% target. Though timing is influenced by markets and the credit environment, we are confident this trajectory can continue and ultimately our targets should be higher. Like all management teams, we are balancing many things, growth, risk, changing interest rate expectations, inflation, and AI opportunities just to name a few. However, our North Star remains the same. Invest in our people, products, technology and marketing for the long-term, but show consistent progress in growing revenue

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and returns in the short-term without taking outsized risks for growing in ways that is not consistent with our long-term vision for Wells Fargo. I'll now turn the call over to Mike. Thank you, Charlie. Good morning, everyone. Since Charlie already covered the key drivers behind our financial performance and the business highlights, I'll begin my remarks on slide four. Our third quarter results demonstrated the progress we've made in strengthening the company's financial performance, strong balance sheet growth, continued revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and solid credit performance drove another quarter of double-digit EPS growth and continued improvement in returns year-over-year. Turning to slide six, net interest income increased

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: 567 million or 5% from a year ago and increased 2% from the second quarter. The growth from the second quarter was driven by higher loan and investment securities balances, one additional day in the quarter, fixed-rate asset repricing, as well as the impact of higher rates on floating-rate assets. The net interest margin was stable from the second quarter as the benefits of loan growth and higher yields in almost all categories of interest-earning assets, including the impact of fixed asset repricing were offset by continued growth in interest-varying deposits. This was a better result than we expected at the beginning of the quarter due to slightly higher cash and securities balances, slightly lower funding costs, and additional efficiency in deployment of the market's balance sheet.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: As we continued to grow the market's balance sheet on a gross basis, we were becoming increasingly more efficient in how we deploy it, and we made more progress this quarter than we originally anticipated. As our equity finance business expands, we are realizing greater netting benefits, and on the fixed-income side, we are implementing more efficient funding structures, including sponsored repo and other balance sheet optimization solutions. I will update you on our expectations for full-year net interest income later on the call. Moving to slide seven, average loans increased 105 billion or 11% from a year ago, driven by growth in commercial and industrial loans where demand remains healthy. Commitment levels have continued to increase across both commercial banking

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and the corporate investment bank, while utilization rates have remained relatively stable. On the consumer side, auto, securities-based lending, and credit card continued to be the primary growth drivers. Turning to deposits, average deposits increased 143 billion or 11% from a year ago, and we're off 1% from the second quarter. We continued to have strong commercial and despairing deposit growth, reflecting continued client demand for higher yielding products, as well as our targeted growth initiatives. Consumer balances increased from a year ago, and with the modest decline in balances from the second quarter reflecting seasonal outflows. Turning to slide eight, non-interest income declined 1% from a year ago.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: We had growth across several categories, including investment advisory, deposit-related fees, investment banking, and card fees, reflecting continued momentum in businesses where we've been investing. However, this growth was more than offset by lower trading gains, although revenue in our markets business was down only slightly versus a year ago. Lower leasing come following the sale of our rail car leasing business in the first quarter, as well as lower gains from the equity securities also contributed to the decline. We had only modest net gains from equity securities in the third quarter, and we currently expect them to remain low in the fourth quarter, as we have highlighted in the past, results from our venture capital investments can be volatile from quarter to quarter, but we continue to expect strong returns over time.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: It's important note that we generated more than one billion of equity gains during the first half of the year, which is in line with our historical full-year average. As a result, even with minimal gains in the second half of the year, we would still be on track for a solid full-year results. Turning new expenses on slide nine, non-interest expense declined 103 million from a year ago, and our efficiency ratio proved to 63% down two percentage points year-to-year. Personnel expense declined during my lower sevens cost, which were 296 million a year ago. Higher revenue related compensation expense was largely offset by the benefits of our efficiency initiatives. Non-personnel expense increased from a year ago driven by higher tech and technology

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and equipment expense, turning to credit quality on slide 10. Our credit performance in the third quarter remained strong with a net loan charge of a ratio of 38 basis points of average loans down from a year ago. Commercial net loan charge offs were stable from a year ago and increased eight basis points from the second quarter to 18 basis points. We continue to monitor for a range of macroeconomic and industry specific risks, including higher interest rates, inflation, geopolitical uncertainty, and AI related disruption. But as of now, we do not see signs of broad-based credit deterioration. Losses continue to be idiosyncratic and driven by borrower specific situations.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Consumer credit performance was strong with good performance across all portfolios and consumer net loan charge offs declined to 70 basis points. Our allowance coverage ratio for total loans was relatively stable compared with the second quarter. Growth in commercial and industrial and auto loan balances drove the modest increase in the allowance, which was largely offset by a lower allowance for commercial real estate office loans. Turning to capital liquidity in slide 11. Our capital levels remained strong with our CET1 ratio at 10% well above our CET1 regulatory minimum plus buffers of 8.5%. The decline from the second quarter included a decrease in accumulated other comprehensive income driven by the impact of higher interest rates.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: We planned to continue to manage our CET1 ratio to be within our targeted range of 10 to 10.5%. During the third quarter, we increased our common stock dividend of 50 cents per share and repurchased 2.5 billion of common stock. Looking ahead, we will continue to consider the interest rate environment and the impact on accumulated other comprehensive income when determining how much stock we repurchase. And as a reminder, we expect the Federal Reserve to finalize Basel III capital rules. And based on the proposal, we have estimated that our risk-weighted assets could decrease by approximately 7%, which all else being equal would increase our CET1 ratio. We provide an update on our operating segments on slides 12 through 15.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Charlie has already covered the key drivers of revenue growth across the businesses, so I'll keep my comments brief and just highlight a few additional points. Let me start with consumer banking and lending. We generated solid revenue growth while reducing expenses and return on allocated capital increased to over 32% in the third quarter. Commercial banking had good revenue growth and combined with disciplined expense management, their efficiency ratio improved to 43% in the third quarter from 48% a year ago. Turning to corporate investment banking, banking revenue was up 8% from a year ago, including a 10% increase in investment banking. I'd like to focus for a moment on our markets business where results can vary with market conditions.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: While equities revenue was up 21% from a year ago, total markets revenue was relatively stable from a year ago, and revenue in the third quarter was not as strong as during the first two quarters of the year. At an industry conference last month, I indicated that we expected third quarter markets revenue to be up mid-single digits a year a year. Our actual results reflected a more challenging market environment late in the quarter than we had anticipated. During the final weeks of September, interest rates moved sharply and these moves pressured fixed income valuations and significantly reduced client activity, particularly in strategic transactions, hedging activity in the primary issuance market. At the same time, equity market volatility stayed low, creating a less favorable environment for our equities derivative franchise.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Finally, turning to wealth and investment management, which generated strong results. I'd like to remind you that the majority of WIM advisory assets are priced at the beginning of the quarter, so fourth quarter results were reflected to October 1st market valuations, which were above both July 1st and a year ago levels. Turning to our 2026 outlook on slide 17, starting with net interest income, we still expect net interest income for full year 2026 to be 50 billion plus or minus. Fourth quarter net interest income is expected to be approximately 13 billion and the net interest margin is expected to be stable from the third quarter. We expect the pace of net interest income growth to increase in the fourth quarter

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: versus the prior two quarters due to a few factors. We expect continued benefits from loan growth as well as deposit growth. We also expect continued benefits from fixed rate asset repricing and higher investment securities balances. Given we are modestly asset sensitive, we expect fourth quarter net interest income excluding markets to benefit from the higher interest rate environment. However, markets, which is liability senses, some of these benefits would be offset since markets net interest income is negatively impacted by higher rates. However, this would largely be offset by markets non-interest income. Turning to expenses, we continue to expect 2026 non-interest expense to be approximately 55.7 billion. While full year revenue related expenses

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: are expected to be approximately 400 million above our original expectations driven by strong business growth and equity markets, our ongoing focus on improving efficiency is training more savings across the company allowing us to offset the higher revenue related expense. Our third quarter results demonstrate the strength of the franchise and the ongoing successful execution of our strategy. We continue to grow earnings, increase returns and invest in the business while maintaining strong credit performance and a disciplined approach to expenses. Our stronger performance during the first three quarters of the year highlights the continued incremental progress we are making towards our goal of higher growth and returns. We will now take your questions. At this time, we will now begin the question

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and answer session. If you would like to ask a question,

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: please first unmute your phone and then press star one.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Please record at your game at the prompt. If you would like to withdraw your question,

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: you may press star two to remove yourself

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: from the question queue.

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: Once again, please press star one and record your name

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: if you would like to ask a question at this time. Please stand by for our first question. And our first question will come from John McDonald of Truist Securities.

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: Your line is open, sir.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Thank you. Good morning. Mike, I was hoping you could start off maybe just repeat a little bit of the comments about the drivers of the net interesting income growth that you expect in the fourth quarter. And then maybe just clarify what you were saying about markets and versus non-markets, maybe in the context of I think for the full year, you originally were hoping for 48 and two to get to the 50. Is that still the same? And maybe just clarify what you're saying about, you know, the fourth quarter split, maybe between markets and total NII. Yeah. Hey John, thanks for the question. And so let me just start a little bit on Q3 and then I'll quickly bridge into Q4.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: So what we saw in Q3 is the agri-git NIM stabilized. But when you look beneath that a little bit, what was happening is the NIMX markets increased slightly. So we saw a little bit of expansion there. And that's part of what you're gonna see as you go into Q4 as well. And then we also got the benefit of a lot of the efficiency work we've been doing and how we deploy the balance sheet in the markets business. And that sort of helps like bring good stability, I think overall to the NIM. And so we still expect that to be flat in Q4 relative to Q3. And just to double click on that one second. So when you look at what we did in markets,

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: is I think fixed income financing is a good illustration of it. The gross financing balances, they grew about 18% from the second quarter. But the net balances were down. And that was a lot of the optimization that we have been doing, moving more clients to sponsor repo and other things. But, and so we've got really good confidence that we've got more ability to continue to do that. And that'll be pretty stable. So that's sort of underpins sort of the, the NIM being pretty stable as we go into Q4. What's happening in Q4 then is you start to get the benefits of a lot of what you started seeing in Q3.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: So, look at loan balances. The step off into Q4 is bigger than obviously the average balances you saw in the quarter. I think we were up the end of periods up 15 billion or so, going into the fourth quarter. You have to look through a little bit of that because there's a little bit of seasonality at the end of the quarter in the commercial bank. But nonetheless, the step up is bigger. And so you're getting the benefit of that in the fourth quarter. We continue to grow deposits. And so you'll see more of that contribute into the quarter as well. You've got the benefit of rates and sort of yield and repricing sort of coming through in the balance sheet.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: So almost every category outside of the market's business of earning assets, saw a little bit of benefit in Q3 from higher yields. And you're going to see more of that in Q4. And that's going to lead to a little bit more of an expansion of the NIMX markets as well as you go into the quarter. And then there are a few other factors that sort of drive it. But those are sort of the big ones that sort of lead to the step up that we're going to see going into Q4. And what I was saying on the markets that I eye is as you go into this rising rate environment,

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: we're asset sensitive on the banking book. You're going to see that NIMX span. You're going to see sort of the impact of rates come through. And since markets is liability sensitive, you're going to see some impact on markets, NII going into the fourth quarter. But that'll be offset in fees. And then when you look at the mix of the 50 billion, our best guess is on the markets, NII that it'll be slightly below 2 billion, call it 1.8 ish. And then you'll make up for some of it to get in the non-markets, NII to sort of get back to the full year of 50 billion. Okay, thanks. That's really helpful.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: And it's too early for guidance on 2027 NII, but any early thoughts in terms of kind of just the drivers the next year's NII relative to where you think you'll jump off on the fourth quarter, things we should keep in mind. Good guys, bad guys, as you go through your planning. Yeah, I mean, like certainly when you look at the step off point coming out of Q4, that's a net positive sort of where we are. Rates appear to be either increasing or certainly staying higher for longer than we contemplated not that long ago. So that's a net positive. We're still seeing good growth across the loan portfolios. We expect to continue to see good growth

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: in the card business, auto business, as well as on the commercial side. So those all be positive. And then we've been pretty successful like growing deposits, particularly the interest bearing deposits. And so I think all of those things should sort of continue as we go into next year with all the right caveats around sort of, the macro environment sort of being pretty constructive despite some of the noise you have there. But we enter the year. And I think if you know the 13 billion is what close to $700 million over last year. And so you sort of enter the year in a better place. Okay, got it. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Operator
segments.text: Next question will come from Scott Ceefers of TD Cowan. Your line is open.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: Morning guys, thanks for taking the question. Mike or Charlie was hoping you could maybe just sort of touch on sort of your thoughts for how a period of sustained higher rates kind of changes your sense for, you know, both customer health and resilience. And then maybe also touch on sort of your sense for how commercial demand might change portions of the consumer book where you've had good growth, how that might change, et cetera. So, you know, basically impact on sort of resilience and growth dynamics. Hey Scott, it's Mike. I'll take a shot and welcome back. I think, oh, really good. Oh, thank you. And then you new seat. So I, you know, like I think we've been living in this environment now for a while where, you know, inflation's been higher,

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: rates have been pretty high, you know, although, you know, have moved a little bit higher more recently, you've seen, you know, the and the cumulative impact of that has been flowing through, you know, the economy. But what we're seeing sort of offset some of, you know, what would be, you know, kind of the negatives is, is wages and employment continues to be really strong. Wages are largely keeping up with inflation. You know, even at all of the different cohorts of clients we have, when you look at them, income levels, wealth levels, the data would say on a cumulative basis over the last number of years, wages have sort of kept up, which is sort of supporting supporting the activity levels that we're seeing.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: We're seeing, you know, we're not seeing any, any like deterioration in the credit profile of the consumer. So I think as long as the unemployment picture stays pretty strong, like, you know, we should be able to keep seeing sort of the, the strong activity levels and strong performance across the consumer base. And, you know, even when you start looking at energy and gas prices, you know, it is meaningful for sure, but it ends up being three to 6% of spend depending on your wealth level or income level. So it's still, you know, manageable, you know, and people who are able to offset, you know, other offset that, you know, with, you know, with savings and other categories of spend. So overall, we're seeing, you know, a pretty strong picture there. And as long as the economy continues to grow

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: and employment stays strong, that should, you know, continue and we're just not seeing signs of that changing at this point, either from, you know, the way our, the sentiment across our commercial client base or just in the actual metrics that we're seeing, you know, in on the consumer side. On the commercial side, you know, rates are rates, you know, higher rates definitely matter. But, you know, in many of our, you know, commercial banking type clients, you know, people have been pretty prudent now for a while, for years, you know, in terms of how much leverage they're putting on. So they're still being, you know, thoughtful about inventory levels or levels of investment, despite sort of, you know, the AI and, you know, CapEx cycle that Charlie sort of talked about a little bit.

segments.speaker: Management
segments.text: So they come into this environment in pretty good shape. Now, the higher rates are definitely going to impact valuations in places like commercial real estate. But that'll take some time to really kind of play through those asset classes.
